summary: Milestone 2026.04.99 closeout was a short 10 minute operational slice with 2 completed items. The only material slow path was the 10 minute arXiv Bundle v10 step gated on Exp 1269 critical paper fixes. GPUs were idle at closeout with no material zombie processes, pre-flight checks were seconds-scale, and the main recoverable loss is serial gate/docs execution plus unused DualGPU capacity.

slowest_experiments.name: arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_slow: The bundle could not start until Exp 1269 paper-critical fixes were complete, then had to run the TeX compile and bundle packaging path. It consumed effectively all measured closeout wall time.

slowest_experiments.name: In-process docs for arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_slow: No material wall time was attributed in the supplied timing block; docs were not the measured bottleneck in this slice.

gpu_state.efficiency_assessment: Inefficient for any GPU-capable work: both RTX 3090s were idle throughout closeout observation. This slice was mostly CPU/docs/TeX bound, but future GPU tasks should be scheduled in parallel via DualGPURunner rather than allowed to close with both devices idle.

evidence: ops/conductor-log.md recorded Exp 1269 pre-flight as 81 passed, 1 warning in 8.24s.
ops/conductor-log.md recorded Exp 1270 pre-flight as 81 passed, 1 warning in 7.89s.
preflight_assessment.assessment: Pre-flight was not the limiting factor for this 10 minute slice; it was under 2 minutes total and closer to seconds-scale overhead.

doc_reconciliation_assessment.assessment: The supplied timing block assigns 0 minutes to in-process docs, so docs were not the measured bottleneck. However, the repeated .99 changelog/roadmap closeout entries show that docs reconciliation still needs idempotent deduplication to avoid repeated agent passes.

parallelization_assessment.details: The gated arXiv bundle itself was serial on Exp 1269, but docs reconciliation, GPU-capable downstream experiments, and independent audit/reporting work could run in separate CPU/GPU lanes. A conductor scheduler should keep TeX/docs on CPU while launching eligible Qwen/Gemma jobs on GPU 0/1.

bottlenecks_identified: Single serial critical path: Exp 1270 arXiv Bundle v10 waited on Exp 1269 and consumed the entire measured nonzero closeout duration.
DualGPU capacity was unused at closeout: both RTX 3090s were at 4 MB and 0% utilization.
No material GPU zombie was present, but the 4 MB idle allocations triggered cleanup suggestions and should be treated as low-priority hygiene.
Docs reconciliation was not slow in the supplied timing, but repeated .99 operational entries indicate idempotency/deduplication friction.
Pre-flight was not a bottleneck in this slice; focused 81-test checks completed in 8.24s and 7.89s.
Conductor timing granularity is too coarse: a 0 minute docs slot hides whether the pass was skipped, cached, or simply rounded down.
improvements_suggested: Make the conductor GPU-aware by default: schedule independent Qwen work on GPU 0 and Gemma work on GPU 1 whenever both devices are idle.
Split gated publication work into explicit sub-steps: gate check, TeX compile, bundle packaging, upload-blocker recording, and docs reconciliation.
Cache TeX dependencies and compile artifacts between arXiv bundle retries so repeated bundle checks do not redownload or rerun unnecessary steps.
Emit structured gate-block artifacts immediately when prerequisites are missing, rather than spending a full experiment slot proving the gate is blocked.
Make docs reconciliation idempotent: detect an existing same-milestone roadmap row and changelog paragraph before writing another closeout summary.
Record per-experiment timings with second-level precision, including pre-flight, implementation, verification, artifact write, and docs phases.
Run GPU monitor snapshots at experiment start and finish and attach process lists to the result artifact.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add a GPU-aware parallel lane scheduler that keeps CPU/docs/TeX work separate from DualGPU inference/training slots.
Introduce structured timing fields for each conductor phase so 0 minute or rounded slots cannot hide docs, gate, or compile overhead.
Make docs and roadmap reconciliation idempotent with duplicate detection keyed by milestone and theme.
estimated_time_savings_rationale: A 30% saving is realistic for the next similar closeout: overlap independent CPU/GPU work with publication gating, cache TeX and focused pre-flight state, emit immediate structured gate-block artifacts, and make docs reconciliation idempotent. On a 10 minute slice this is only about 3 minutes, but the same fixes matter more when a milestone has many queued tasks.

questions_answered.which_experiments_took_longest_and_why: Exp 1270, arXiv Bundle v10, took 10 minutes because it was gated on Exp 1269 critical paper fixes and then performed the compile/bundle path. The docs slot registered 0 minutes and was not material.
questions_answered.was_gpu_utilization_efficient: No. Both RTX 3090s were idle at 0% utilization with only 4 MB allocated each. The slice did not use DualGPURunner parallelism.
questions_answered.were_zombie_processes_wasting_resources: No material zombies were detected. scripts/gpu_monitor.py reported no GPU processes; the 4 MB idle allocations are hygiene noise, not a >1 GB zombie under monitor thresholds.
questions_answered.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: Yes. The bundle was serial on its prerequisite, but docs, monitoring, and independent GPU-capable work could have run in parallel CPU/GPU lanes.
questions_answered.was_preflight_test_suite_a_bottleneck: No. Relevant conductor rows show focused checks passing in 8.24s and 7.89s.
questions_answered.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: Mostly for this slice because timing recorded 0 minutes, but repeated .99 docs entries show reconciliation is not idempotent enough.
questions_answered.what_tooling_infrastructure_changes_woul: GPU-aware scheduling, structured per-phase timing, cached TeX/pre-flight state, immediate gate-block artifacts, idempotent docs reconciliation, and start/end GPU monitor attachments.

meta_reflection: This milestone's operational lesson is not that the research tasks were too large; it is that a very small closeout still allowed a serial publication gate and idle accelerator capacity to dominate the process. The next milestone should optimize orchestration first: parallel lanes, precise timing, and idempotent reconciliation.
